paragraphs.sourceText: When you look up at the night sky, what do you see? There are other 26 bodies out there besides the moon and stars. One of the most 27 of these is a comet (彗星).
Comets were formed around the same time the Earth was formed. They are 28 ice and other frozen liquids and gases. 29 these “dirty snowballs” begin to orbit the sun, just as the planets do.

As a comet gets closer to the sun, some gases in it begin to unfreeze. They 30 dust particles from the comet to form a huge cloud. As the comet gets even nearer to the sun, a solar wind blows the cloud behind the comet, thus forming its tail. The tail and the 31 fuzzy (模糊的）atmosphere around a comet are 32 that can help identify this 33 in the night sky.

In any given year, about a dozen known comets come close to the sun in their orbits. The average person can’t see them all, of course. Usually there is only one or two a year bright enough to be seen with the 34 eye. Comet Hale-Bopp, discovered in 1995, was an unusually bright comet. Its orbit brought it 35 close to the Earth, within 122 million miles of it. But Hale-Bopp came a long way on its earthly visit. It won’t be back for another four thousand years or so.

paragraphs.sourceText: Scholars of the information society are divided over whether social inequality decreases or increases in an information-based society. However, they generally agree with the idea that inequality in the information society is 36 different from that of an industrial society. As informatization progresses in society, the cause and structural nature of social inequality changes as well.

It seems that the information society 37 the quantity of information available to the members of a society by revolutionizing the ways of using and exchanging information. But such a view is a 38 analysis based on the quantity of information supplied by various forms of the mass media. A different 39 is possible when the actual amount of information 40 by the user is taken into account. In fact, the more information 41 throughout the entire society, the wider the gap becomes between “information haves” and “information have-nots”, leading to digital divide.

According to recent studies, digital divide has been caused by three major 42 ：class, sex, and generation. In terms of class, digital divide exists among different types of workers and between the upper and middle classes and the lower class. With 43 to sex, digital divide exists between men and women. The greatest gap, however, is between the Net-generation, 44 with personal computers and the Internet, and the older generation, 45 to an industrial society.

paragraphs.sourceText: Joy ：A Subject Schools Lack
paragraphs.translationZh: 快乐：学校缺乏的科目

paragraphs.sourceText: Becoming educated should not require giving up pleasure.
paragraphs.translationZh: 受教育不应该要求放弃快乐。

paragraphs.sourceText: A) When Jonathan Swift proposed, in 1729, that the people of Ireland eat their children, he insisted it would solve three problems at once：feed the hungry masses, reduce the population during a severe depression, and stimulate the restaurant business. Even as a satire (讽刺), it seems disgusting and shocking in America with its child-centered culture. But actually, the country is closer to his proposal than you might think.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 1729 年，当乔纳森·斯威夫特 (Jonathan Swift) 提议爱尔兰人民吃自己的孩子时，他坚持认为这会立即解决三个问题：养活饥饿的群众、减少严重萧条期间的人口以及刺激餐馆生意。即使作为讽刺，在以儿童为中心的文化的美国，这也显得令人厌恶和震惊。但实际上，这个国家比你想象的更接近他的提议。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) If you spend much time with educators and policy makers, you’ll hear a lot of the following words ： “ standards,”“ results,”“ skills,”“ self-control,”“ accountability,” and so on. I have visited some of the newer supposedly “effective” schools, where children shout slogans in order to learn self- control or must stand behind their desk when they can’t sit still.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 如果你花很多时间与教育工作者和政策制定者打交道，你会听到很多以下词语：“标准”、“结果”、“技能”、“自我控制”、“责任”等等。我参观过一些据说“高效”的新学校，孩子们通过喊口号来学习自我控制，或者当他们坐不住时必须站在桌子后面。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) A look at what goes on in most classrooms these days makes it abundantly clear that when people think about education, they are not thinking about what it feels like to be a child, or what makes childhood an important and valuable stage of life in its own right.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 看看现在大多数教室里发生的事情就可以清楚地看出，当人们考虑教育时，他们并没有考虑作为一个孩子的感觉，或者是什么让童年本身成为一个重要而有价值的人生阶段。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) I’m a mother of three, a teacher, and a developmental psychologist. So I’ve watched a lot of children—talking, playing, arguing, eating, studying, and being young. Here’s what I’ve come to understand. The thing that sets children apart from adults is not their ignorance, nor their lack of skills. It’s their enormous capacity for joy. Think of a 3-year-old lost in the pleasures of finding out what he can and cannot sink in the bathtub, a 5-year-old beside herself with the thrill of putting together strings of nonsensical words with her best friends, or an 11-year-old completely absorbed in a fascinating comic strip. A child’s ability to become deeply absorbed in something, and derive intense pleasure from that absorption, is something adults spend the rest of their lives trying to return to.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 我是三个孩子的母亲、一名教师和一名发展心理学家。所以我见过很多孩子——说话、玩耍、争论、吃饭、学习和小时候。这是我的理解。儿童与成人的不同之处不是他们无知，也不是他们缺乏技能。这是他们巨大的快乐能力。想象一下，一个 3 岁的孩子沉浸在寻找自己可以和什么不能沉入浴缸的乐趣中，一个 5 岁的孩子因与她最好的朋友拼出一串串无意义的单词而兴奋不已，或者一个 11 岁的孩子完全沉浸在迷人的漫画中。孩子能够深深地专注于某件事，并从这种专注中获得强烈的快乐，这是成年人一生都在努力恢复的能力。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) A friend told me the following story. One day, when he went to get his 7-year-old son from soccer practice, his kid greeted him with a downcast face and a sad voice. The coach had criticized him for not focusing on his soccer drills. The little boy walked out of the school with his head and shoulders hanging down. He seemed wrapped in sadness. But just before he reached the car door, he suddenly stopped, crouching (蹲伏) down to peer at something on the sidewalk. His face went down lower and lower, and then, with complete joy he called out, “Dad. Come here. This is the strangest bug I’ve ever seen. It has, like, a million legs. Look at this. It’s amazing. ” He looked up at his father, his features overflowing with energy and delight. “ Can’t we stay here for just a minute? I want to find out what he does with all those legs. This is the coolest ever. ”
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 一位朋友告诉我以下故事。有一天，当他去接7岁的儿子结束足球训练时，他的孩子一脸沮丧，声音悲伤。教练批评他没有专注于足球训练。小男孩低着头、低着肩膀走出了学校。他似乎沉浸在悲伤之中。但就在他走到车门前时，他突然停了下来，蹲下身子，盯着人行道上的什么东西。他的脸越来越低，然后满心喜悦地喊道：“爸爸。过来。这是我见过的最奇怪的虫子。它好像有一百万条腿。看看这个。太神奇了。”他抬头看着父亲，脸上洋溢着活力和喜悦。 “我们就不能在这里呆一分钟吗？我想看看他用这些腿做了什么。这是有史以来最酷的。”

paragraphs.sourceText: F) The traditional view of such moments is that they constitute a charming but irrelevant byproduct of youth—something to be pushed aside to make room for more important qualities, like perseverance (坚持不懈）, obligation, and practicality. Yet moments like this one are just the kind of intense absorption and pleasure adults spend the rest of their lives seeking. Human lives are governed by the desire to experience joy. Becoming educated should not require giving up joy but rather lead to finding joy in new kinds of things: reading novels instead of playing with small figures, conducting experiments instead of sinking cups in the bathtub, and debating serious issues rather than stringing together nonsense words, for example. In some cases, schools should help children find new, more grown-up ways of doing the same things that are constant sources of joy：making art, making friends, making decisions.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 对这些时刻的传统看法是，它们构成了青春时期一种迷人但无关紧要的副产品——应该被抛在一边，为更重要的品质腾出空间，比如坚持不懈、义务和务实。然而，像这样的时刻正是成年人用余生寻求的一种强烈的专注和快乐。人类的生活是由体验快乐的欲望所支配的。受教育不应该要求放弃快乐，而应该导致在新的事物中找到快乐：读小说而不是玩游戏例如，培养小人物、进行实验而不是把杯子沉进浴缸、辩论严肃的问题而不是胡说八道。在某些情况下，学校应该帮助孩子们找到新的、更成熟的方式来做同样的事情，这些事情是持续的快乐源泉：创作艺术、结交朋友、做决定。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Building on a child’s ability to feel joy, rather than pushing it aside, wouldn’t be that hard. It would just require a shift in the education world’s mindset（思维模式）. Instead of trying to get children to work hard, why not focus on getting them to take pleasure in meaningful, productive activity, like making things, working with others, exploring ideas, and solving problems? These focuses are not so different from the things in which they delight.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 培养孩子感受快乐的能力，而不是将其推到一边，并不那么难。这只需要教育界思维模式的转变。与其试图让孩子们努力工作，为什么不专注于让他们享受有意义的、富有成效的活动，比如制作东西、与他人合作、探索想法和解决问题呢？这些焦点与他们所喜欢的事物并没有太大不同。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Before you brush this argument aside as rubbish, or think of joy as an unaffordable luxury in a nation where there is awful poverty, low academic achievement, and high dropout rates, think again. The more horrible the school circumstances, the more important pleasure is to achieving any educational success.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 在你把这个论点当作垃圾抛在一边，或者认为在一个极度贫困、学业成绩低下、辍学率高的国家里，快乐是一种负担不起的奢侈品之前，请再想一想。学校环境越糟糕，获得教育成功的快乐就越重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Many of the assignments and rules teachers come up with, often because they are pressured by their administrators, treat pleasure and joy as the enemies of competence and responsibility. The assumption is that children shouldn’t chat in the classroom because it hinders hard work；instead, they should learn to delay gratification(快乐）so that they can pursue abstract goals, like going to college.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 教师提出的许多作业和规则，往往是因为他们受到管理者的压力，将快乐和喜悦视为能力和责任的敌人。我们的假设是，孩子们不应该在课堂上聊天，因为这会妨碍努力工作；相反，他们应该学会延迟满足（快乐），以便他们可以追求抽象的目标，比如上大学。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Not only is this a boring and awful way to treat children, it makes no sense educationally. Decades of research have shown that in order to acquire skills and real knowledge in school, kids need to want to learn. You can force a child to stay in his or her seat, fill out a worksheet, or practice division. But you can’t force the child to think carefully, enjoy books, digest complex information, or develop a taste for learning. To make that happen, you have to help the child find pleasure in learning—to see school as a source of joy.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 这不仅是一种无聊而可怕的对待孩子的方式，而且在教育上毫无意义。数十年的研究表明，为了在学校获得技能和真正的知识，孩子们需要有学习的欲望。您可以强迫孩子留在座位上、填写工作表或练习除法。但你不能强迫孩子仔细思考、享受书籍、消化复杂的信息或培养学习的品味。为了实现这一目标，你必须帮助孩子找到学习的乐趣——将学校视为快乐的源泉。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Adults tend to talk about learning as if it were medicine: unpleasant, but necessary and good for you. Why not instead think of learning as if it were food—something so valuable to humans that they have evolved to experience it as a pleasure?
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 成年人倾向于谈论学习，就好像它是一种药物：令人不快，但必要且对你有好处。为什么不把学习当作食物——这对人类来说非常有价值，以至于他们已经进化到将学习当作一种乐趣呢？

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Joy should not be trained out of children or left for after-school programs. The more difficult a child’s life circumstances, the more important it is for that child to find joy in his or her classroom. “Pleasure” is not a dirty word. And it doesn’t run counter to the goals of public education. It is, in fact, the precondition.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 不应培养孩子的快乐或将其留给课外活动。孩子的生活环境越困难，孩子在课堂上找到快乐就越重要。 “快乐”并不是一个肮脏的词。这并不违背公共教育的目标。事实上，这是前提。

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. It will not be difficult to make learning a source of joy if educators change their way of thinking.
paragraphs.translationZh: 46. 如果教育者改变思维方式，让学习成为快乐的源泉并不困难。

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. What distinguishes children from adults is their strong ability to derive joy from what they are doing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 儿童与成人的区别在于他们从所做的事情中获得快乐的能力很强。

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. Children in America are being treated with shocking cruelty.
paragraphs.translationZh: 48. 美国的儿童正在遭受令人震惊的残酷对待。

paragraphs.sourceText: 49. It is human nature to seek joy in life.
paragraphs.translationZh: 49. 寻求生活乐趣是人的本性。

paragraphs.sourceText: 50. Grown-ups are likely to think that learning to children is what medicine is to patients.
paragraphs.translationZh: 50. 成年人可能认为学习之于孩子就像医学之于病人。

paragraphs.sourceText: 51. Bad school conditions make it all the more important to turn learning into a joyful experience.
paragraphs.translationZh: 51. 糟糕的学校条件使得将学习变成快乐的经历变得更加重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: 52. Adults do not consider children’s feelings when it comes to education.
paragraphs.translationZh: 52.成人在教育方面不考虑孩子的感受。

paragraphs.sourceText: 53. Administrators seem to believe that only hard work will lead children to their educational goals.
paragraphs.translationZh: 53. 管理者似乎相信，只有努力工作才能引导孩子们实现他们的教育目标。

paragraphs.sourceText: 54. In the so-called “effective” schools, children are taught self-control under a set of strict rules.
paragraphs.translationZh: 54. 在所谓的“有效”学校中，儿童在一套严格的规则下接受自我控制教育。

paragraphs.sourceText: 55. To make learning effective, educators have to ensure that children want to learn.
paragraphs.translationZh: 55. 为了使学习有效，教育工作者必须确保儿童愿意学习。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 56 to 60 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 56 至 60 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: When it’s five o’clock, people leave their office. The length of the workday, for many workers, is defined by time. They leave when the clock tells them they’re done.
paragraphs.translationZh: 到了五点钟，人们就离开了办公室。对于许多工人来说，工作日的长度是由时间决定的。当时钟告诉他们完成时，他们就离开了。

paragraphs.sourceText: These days, the time is everywhere: not just on clocks or watches, but on cell-phones and computers. That may be a bad thing, particularly at work. New research shows that clock-based work schedules hinder morale (士气) and creativity.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如今，时间无处不在：不仅在钟表上，而且在手机和电脑上。这可能是一件坏事，尤其是在工作中。新的研究表明，基于时钟的工作时间表会阻碍士气和创造力。

paragraphs.sourceText: Clock-timers organize their day by blocks of minutes and hours. For example：a meeting from 9 a. m. to 10 a. m. , research from 10 a. m. to noon, etc. On the other hand, task-timers have a list of things they want to accomplish. They work down the list, each task starts when the previous task is completed. It is said that all of us employ a mix of both these types of planning.
paragraphs.translationZh: 时钟计时器按照分钟和小时来安排他们的一天。例如：上午 9 点开会。米。到 10 a。米。 ，从上午 10 点开始研究。米。到中午等。另一方面，任务计时器有一个他们想要完成的事情的清单。他们按照列表进行工作，每个任务在前一个任务完成后开始。据说我们所有人都混合使用了这两种类型的计划。

paragraphs.sourceText: What, then, are the effects of thinking about time in these different ways? Does one make us more productive? Better at the tasks at hand? Happier? In experiments conducted by Tamar Avnet and Anne-Laure Sellier, they had participants organize different activities—from project planning, holiday shopping, to yoga —by time or to-do list to measure how they performed under “clock time vs “task time.” They found clock timers to be more efficient but less happy because they felt little control over their lives. Task timers are happier and more creative, but less productive. They tend to enjoy the moment when something good is happening, and seize opportunities that come up.
paragraphs.translationZh: 那么，以这些不同的方式思考时间会产生什么影响呢？它能让我们更有生产力吗？更好地完成手头的任务？更快乐吗？在 Tamar Avnet 和 Anne-Laure Sellier 进行的实验中，他们让参与者按时间或待办事项列表组织不同的活动（从项目规划、假日购物到瑜伽），以衡量他们在“时钟时间与”任务时间”下的表现。他们发现时钟计时器效率更高，但不太快乐，因为他们感觉自己无法控制自己的生活。任务计时器更快乐，更有创造力，但生产力较低。他们倾向于享受好事发生的时刻，并抓住出现的机会。

paragraphs.sourceText: The researchers argue that task-based organizing tends to be undervalued and under-supported in business culture. Smart companies, they believe, will try to bake more task-based planning into their strategies.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究人员认为，基于任务的组织在商业文化中往往被低估和支持不足。他们相信，聪明的公司会尝试将更多基于任务的规划纳入其战略中。

paragraphs.sourceText: This might be a small change to the way we view work and the office, but the researchers argue that it challenges a widespread characteristic of the economy: work organized by dock time. While most people will still probably need, and be, to some extent, clock-timers, task-based timing should be used when perfoming a job that requires more creativity. It’ll make those tasks easier, arid the task- doers will be happier.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这可能只是我们看待工作和办公室的方式的一个小小的改变，但研究人员认为，它挑战了经济的一个普遍特征：按码头时间组织工作。虽然大多数人可能仍然需要并且在某种程度上是时钟计时器，但在执行需要更多创造力的工作时，应该使用基于任务的计时。它会让这些任务变得更容易，任务执行者也会更快乐。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 61 to 65 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 61 至 65 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Martha Stewart was charged, tried and competed of a crime in 2004. As she neared the end of her prison sentence, a well-known columnist wrote that she was “ paying her dues,” and that “ there is simply no reason for anyone to attempt to deny her right to start anew.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 玛莎·斯图尔特 (Martha Stewart) 于 2004 年被指控、审判并参与犯罪活动。当她刑期即将结束时，一位著名专栏作家写道，她正在“偿还应得的费用”，并且“任何人都没有理由试图否认她重新开始的权利”。

paragraphs.sourceText: Surely, the American ideal of second chances should not be reserved only for the rich and powerful. Unfortunately, many federal and state laws impose post-conviction restrictions on a shockingly large number of Americans, who are prevented from ever fully paying their debt to society.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当然，美国的第二次机会理想不应该只为富人和有权势的人保留。不幸的是，许多联邦和州法律对数量惊人的美国人施加了定罪后限制，使他们无法完全偿还对社会的债务。

paragraphs.sourceText: At least 65 million people in the United States have a criminal record. This can result in severe penalties that continue long after punishment is completed.
paragraphs.translationZh: 美国至少有 6500 万人有犯罪记录。这可能会导致严厉的处罚，并且在处罚结束后仍会持续很长时间。

paragraphs.sourceText: Many of these penalties are imposed regardless of the seriousness of the offense or the person’s individual circumstances. Laws can restrict or ban voting, access to public housing, and professional and business licensing. They can affect a person’s ability to get a job and qualification for benefits.
paragraphs.translationZh: 其中许多处罚的实施与罪行的严重程度或个人情况无关。法律可以限制或禁止投票、获得公共住房以及专业和商业许可。它们会影响一个人获得工作的能力和领取福利的资格。

paragraphs.sourceText: In all, more than 45, 000 laws and rules serve to exclude vast numbers of people from fully participating in American life. Some laws make sense. No one advocates letting someone convicted of pedophilia（恋童癖）work in a school. But too often collateral(附随的）consequences bear no relation to public safety. Should a woman who possessed a small amount of drugs years ago be permanently unable to be licensed as a nurse?
paragraphs.translationZh: 总共有超过 45, 000 条法律和规则阻碍了大批人充分参与美国生活。有些法律是有道理的。没有人主张让被判有恋童癖的人在学校工作。但附带后果往往与公共安全无关。多年前拥有少量毒品的女性是否应该永远无法获得护士执照？

paragraphs.sourceText: These laws are also counterproductive, since they make it harder for people with criminal records to find housing or land a job, two key factors that reduce backsliding.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这些法律也会适得其反，因为它们使有犯罪记录的人更难找到住房或找到工作，而这是减少倒退的两个关键因素。

paragraphs.sourceText: A recent report makes several recommendations, including the abolition of most post-conviction penalties, except for those specifically needed to protect public safety. Where the penalties are not a must, they should be imposed only if the facts of a case support it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 最近的一份报告提出了几项建议，包括废除大多数定罪后处罚，但保护公共安全特别需要的处罚除外。不需要处罚的，有事实依据的，才可以处罚。

paragraphs.sourceText: The point is not to excuse or forget the crime. Rather, it is to recognize that in America’s vast criminal justice system, second chances are crucial. It is in no one’s interest to keep a large segment of the population on the margins of society.
paragraphs.translationZh: 重点不是要原谅或忘记罪行。相反，它是要认识到在美国庞大的刑事司法系统中，第二次机会至关重要。让大部分人口处于社会边缘不符合任何人的利益。

options.translationZh: 岗位评价应当采用科学的标准。

options.sourceText: Her past record might stand in her way to a new life.
options.reflowSourceText: Her past record might stand in her way to a new life.
options.translationZh: 她过去的记录可能会阻碍她的新生活。

options.sourceText: Her business went bankrupt while she was in prison.
options.reflowSourceText: Her business went bankrupt while she was in prison.
options.translationZh: 在她入狱期间，她的生意破产了。

options.sourceText: Her release from prison has drawn little attention.
options.reflowSourceText: Her release from prison has drawn little attention.
options.translationZh: 她出狱后并没有引起多少关注。

options.sourceText: Her prison sentence might have been extended.
options.reflowSourceText: Her prison sentence might have been extended.
options.translationZh: 她的刑期可能会被延长。

options.sourceText: They backslide after serving their terms in prison.
options.reflowSourceText: They backslide after serving their terms in prison.
options.translationZh: 他们在监狱服刑后倒退了。

options.sourceText: They are deprived of chances to turn over a new leaf.
options.reflowSourceText: They are deprived of chances to turn over a new leaf.
options.translationZh: 他们被剥夺了改过自新的机会。

options.sourceText: They receive severe penalties for committing minor offenses.
options.reflowSourceText: They receive severe penalties for committing minor offenses.
options.translationZh: 他们因犯下轻微罪行而受到严厉处罚。

options.sourceText: They are convicted regardless of their individual circumstances.
options.reflowSourceText: They are convicted regardless of their individual circumstances.
options.translationZh: 无论个人情况如何，他们都会被定罪。

options.sourceText: They remain poor for the rest of their lives.
options.reflowSourceText: They remain poor for the rest of their lives.

options.sourceText: They are deprived of all social benefits.
options.reflowSourceText: They are deprived of all social benefits.
options.translationZh: 他们被剥夺了所有社会福利。

options.sourceText: They are marginalized in society.
options.reflowSourceText: They are marginalized in society.
options.translationZh: 他们在社会中处于边缘地位。

options.sourceText: They are deserted by their family.
options.reflowSourceText: They are deserted by their family.

options.sourceText: They help to maintain social stability.
options.reflowSourceText: They help to maintain social stability.
options.translationZh: 他们有助于维护社会稳定。

options.sourceText: Some of them have long been outdated.
options.reflowSourceText: Some of them have long been outdated.

options.sourceText: They are hardly understood by the public.
options.reflowSourceText: They are hardly understood by the public.

options.sourceText: A lot of them have negative effects on society.
options.reflowSourceText: A lot of them have negative effects on society.
options.translationZh: 其中很多对社会产生了负面影响。

options.sourceText: To create opportunities for criminals to reform themselves.
options.reflowSourceText: To create opportunities for criminals to reform themselves.
options.translationZh: 为犯罪分子改造自我创造机会。

options.sourceText: To appeal for changes in America’s criminal justice system.
options.reflowSourceText: To appeal for changes in America’s criminal justice system.
options.translationZh: 呼吁改变美国刑事司法系统。

options.sourceText: To ensure that people with a criminal record live a decent life.
options.reflowSourceText: To ensure that people with a criminal record live a decent life.
options.translationZh: 确保有犯罪记录的人过上体面的生活。

options.sourceText: To call people’s attention to prisoners’ conditions in America.
options.reflowSourceText: To call people’s attention to prisoners’ conditions in America.
options.translationZh: 呼吁人们关注美国囚犯的状况。
